Our head trainer brought up something about carrier checks after reading your comments, and I am responding for the Companion Animal Travel Desk to address your concern that your pet was handled in a manner that felt inconsistent with our care standards during the departure disruption. We recognize that a delay can increase stress for both traveler and animal, and our first duty is to keep companion animals calm, secure, and moving through the process with as little disturbance as possible.

The handling record indicates that the crew followed the expected sequence for a carrier review, but your report suggests that the communication around that review did not meet the standard of clarity you should receive. In these cases, the correct approach is to confirm the carrier condition, verify that the animal remains settled, and coordinate with the gate and ramp teams so that each step is explained in plain terms. If any part of that process was rushed or insufficiently communicated, we treat that as a service failure worthy of review.

<<FACT F109>>

Please be assured that our operations planners are reviewing the full chain of events with the crew involved, including the tone used during the exchange and the manner in which the carrier was assessed. We train handlers to use calm, humane methods around animals, and we expect staff to pause, reassess, and escalate concerns through a stepwise review whenever a situation appears unsettled. That process exists to protect the pet and to give travelers confidence that Aurelia Skyways is acting with care and consistency.

If you are willing, please preserve any boarding documents, reference notes, or photographs from the carrier condition so that we can compare them with the operational report. That material helps us determine whether the issue arose from procedure, communication, or an individual lapse in judgment. Our aim is to restore trust through a practical resolution and to prevent a repeat on future companion travel bookings.

We appreciate the opportunity to review this matter and to improve the service your pet should receive on every journey. Companion Animal Travel Desk
